endorsements.quote: Ongoing monitoring is essential to prevent model degradation —the unintended decline in model performance, accuracy, or safety from improper updates, contaminated training data, or inconsistent validation practices.

Beyond technical performance, monitoring must evaluate physician-AI interaction patterns, as clinicians often over rely on or underutilize AI capabilities,93,94 informing both system design and clinician training.
Therefore, we emphasize that implementing redundant monitoring systems and establishing clear reporting mechanisms is critical to ensure prompt remediation when adverse events inevitably occur.
Therefore, we advocate for constrained agentic AI systems in which clinicians remain in the loop, supported by rigorous evaluation and continuous monitoring using clinically meaningful outcomes.
Therefore, we propose models should also be developed using diverse specialist-confirmed cases in addition to neuropathology.

Fairness has been of particular concern as AI has shown numerous biases,100,101 emphasizing the need for training data from diverse groups as well as ongoing monitoring to identify and quickly mitigate biases based upon the analysis of only socioeconomically privileged populations .

To ensure coherence across the AI lifecycle, the oversight body governing standards would ideally also oversee validation , monitoring, and continuous learning processes discussed in the next section.
Establish liability and indemnification frameworks with legal and regulatory input

unlisted_practices: Conduct continuous real-time monitoring of AI conversational agent interactions for content relevance and dangerous content such as suicidal ideation, automatically triggering human intervention.
Use semi-structured interviews for LLM-based conversational history-taking agents to prevent engagement in irrelevant or dangerous topics.
Curate datasets according to FAIR principles, including comprehensive metadata, clear governance frameworks, and quality control procedures.
Use only high-quality, validated cases from diverse clinical settings for model updates and continuous learning to prevent contaminated updates.
Ground AI decision support in the latest evidence using retrieval-augmented generation with human oversight of knowledge-base updates.
Establish dynamic informed consent processes for dementia patients that evolve with changing decision-making capacity and involve caregivers.
Validate AI decision support with sufficient statistical power against defined gold standards in generalizable clinical populations before real-world implementation.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/framework paper outlining a phased roadmap and recommendations for the responsible design and clinical integration of agentic AI systems in neurodegenerative disease care.
